observation_summary: The SerializationUtils.clone method fails with a ClassNotFoundException when attempting to clone objects that contain references to primitive classes (e.g., int.class).
reasoning_summary: The issue is that the custom ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream's resolveClass method did not correctly handle primitive types. The fix involves implementing a lookup mechanism for primitive classes within the resolveClass method, which is a procedural correction to the class resolution algorithm. This is not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple value assignment, but a refinement of the logic used to resolve class names to Class objects.
evidence_used: The bug report states that SerializationUtils throws ClassNotFoundException when cloning primitive classes.
The fix diff shows the addition of a primitiveTypes map and logic in resolveClass to look up primitive classes if Class.forName fails.
The fix modifies the procedural logic of resolveClass to handle primitive types correctly.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds checks (if cls != null), the core issue is the absence of a mechanism to resolve primitive types, which is an algorithmic deficiency in the class resolution process.
This is a local procedural fix within an existing class, not a design-level capability gap.
